propositions: Per-unit Pandoc conversion in the 884-unit hardening oracle invokes timeout resolution and git-root discovery on every call, launching 886 redundant git-rev-parse subprocesses alongside 884 Pandoc processes.
Timeout resolution at _pandoc_timeout() calls load_config() which invokes repo_root() before its result-cache lookup, causing implicit shell-out for every conversion unit.

Resolving timeout once at render-pass boundary and threading it through optional parameters preserves byte-identical outputs, all 884 real Pandoc calls, and per-unit fallback while reducing git-root discovery from 886 to 3 cold probes.
Direct callers of _render_unit and _convert (test_wiki_render.py monkeypatches and legacy hardening loop) retain safe default timeout behavior when optional parameters are omitted.
Held-out resolution-count oracle validates exactly one _pandoc_timeout() call per three-unit render pass before and after fix, and detects mutation regression with defect-seeded timeout leakage.

Fresh 884-unit paired traces confirm 887 total Popen calls (884 Pandoc + 3 root probes) versus 1,770 (884 Pandoc + 886 root), saving 883 redundant subprocesses with 0.2184s quiet-host time reduction and byte-exact corpus outputs.
